speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please describe the specific symptoms of your gait and limb ataxia, including when they began and how they have progressed. To begin our workup, please list your significant past medical history and any current medications.

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of "looking drunk" and clumsiness suggests significant ataxia. To determine if this is cerebellar or sensory in origin, does the ataxia worsen when you close your eyes, and do you experience any numbness or tingling in your limbs?

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML)

Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, your new onset ataxia is highly suspicious for PML, an opportunistic infection of the CNS. We must confirm this immediately with neuroimaging. REQUEST IMAGES: MRI Brain (without contrast). REQUEST TEST: CSF PCR for JC Virus.
